actions.description: Send one fixed 32 time_step service request to the Webots controller. The service response is the only completion evidence; the action returns no observation and does not prove physical motion or state.
actions.name: step

outputs.description: True when the time_step service returned success=true
outputs.name: advanced

actions.description: Send the fixed 0 time_step request that the upstream Quit path sends before it exits. The clone does not contain the service implementation, so the receipt proves only that the controller answered success; it is not a stop and not a safe state.
actions.name: send_zero_time_step

outputs.description: True when the time_step service returned success=true; this is an acknowledgement, not proof of quiescence
outputs.name: acknowledged

facts.text: The pinned package.xml licence tag is TODO.
The README requires Webots R2021a on Ubuntu 20.04.
The world Robot uses the ros controller with the controller arguments --use-sim-time, --clock and --name=robot.
webots.launch includes the webots_ros webots.launch with mode realtime and the webots_map world.
The world declares an InertialUnit, a GPS and a SickLms291 device on the Robot.
The world declares left_motor and right_motor RotationalMotors on the two wheel hinge joints.
The Webots helper creates a client for the relative service robot/robot/time_step of type webots_ros::set_int and sets the request value to TIME_STEP.
The set_int service response is a single bool success field.
The demo controller constant TIME_STEP is 32.
Webots::ChecktimeStep calls the time_step service and reports failure when the call or the service success flag fails.
Webots::Quit deletes the node handle, sets the time_step request value to 0, calls the service without checking the result, then calls ros::shutdown() and exit(0).
The demo controller loop calls ChecktimeStep while ros::ok() and breaks when it returns nonzero.
The demo controller's /cmd_vel callback converts linear.x and angular.z into left and right wheel speeds and calls updateSpeed().
The gmapping broadcaster includes geometry_msgs/PointStamped and sensor_msgs/Imu headers.
The gmapping broadcaster enables the gps service and subscribes to gps/values.
The GPS callback reads point.x and point.z into the demo's planar state.
The amcl launch starts the gmapping broadcaster and demo_2dnav_move.
The amcl launch also starts move_base with cmd_vel remapped to cmd_vel.
The amcl launch remaps the laser scan to robot/Sick_LMS_291/laser_scan/layer0.
The package CMakeLists builds the demo controller and broadcaster executables.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned responses with no Webots physics, controller loop, pacing or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the declared time_step service and the gps/values subscription and runs no Webots R2021a simulation, physics, controller, sensors or wall-clock loop
the time_step call is answered with a canned success and a placeholder counter; no simulation state advances and the 32 value is the upstream controller constant, not a fake timestep
the GPS point and frame id are placeholders and do not follow a robot pose or trajectory
the upstream controller's TIME_STEP is 32, but the fake declares no timestep and no pacing

no e-stop binding and no safe-state action: the 0-value time_step request is what the Quit path sends, unchecked, just before ros::shutdown() and exit(0); the clone does not contain the service implementation, the demo controller keeps requesting 32 ms steps in its loop, and the wheel velocities set from /cmd_vel (move_base in the amcl launch) persist, so an MHS e-stop latches and reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED
the GPS coordinates carry no unit because the clone states none
in the clone only the robot broadcasters call the gps enable service before they subscribe to robot/gps/values; a deployment without one may leave the topic silent, and the read then fails NOT_READY
the laser, camera, wheel velocity services, /cmd_vel, /vel, robot/odom, TF, keyboard and the navigation stack are NOT COVERED
no ROS graph, rosbridge connection, Webots process or hardware was run; a live deployment needs Webots R2021a, ROS 1 Noetic, the webots_ros controller and an operator-run rosbridge endpoint

measures.description: Read one geometry_msgs/PointStamped sample from the gps/values topic.
measures.name: read_gps

safe_state.description: No acknowledged stop exists: an MHS e-stop only latches the driver, refusing further step requests, and reports MHS.SAFETY.SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED. It sends nothing to Webots; the realtime-mode simulation, the demo controller's own 32 ms time_step requests and the wheel velocities it last set from /cmd_vel continue. The 0 time_step request of the upstream Quit path is not bound: the clone does not show what it does.
